# foreman-plane
### Task governance outside your agent harness — personal-tool grade
**English** · 简体中文
## One sentence

**foreman-plane is a governance plane that runs outside the agent harness.**

execution bodies. What the plane owns is the par

dispatch, dependency gating, objective acceptance and an append-only ledger.

> on disk, so it ou

* **Cross session** — the ledger outlives every conversation.
* **Cross instance** — several agents

share one task graph.
* **Cross day** — a task dispatched today can be resumed tomorrow by any body.
* **Zero intrusion** — the plane is a plain process, no agent framework has to be patched.
Zero third-party dependencies. Python ≥ 3.10, standard library only.
## Why foreman-plane?
| Capability | What it changes |
| **Two-level dependency gate** | A card with `[depends_on]` cannot start until every upstream is te
rminal, passed and accepted. `[needs_api]` is the soft level: a missing artefact is reported, the ta

sk still runs. |
| **Objective acceptance** | Pass and fail are computed from the artefact — `min_by

tes`, `sha256`, `contains`, `exit_code`. A task that promises a report but writes no file fails. |
|
**No ghost dispatch** | A card stopped by the gate writes a `blocked` event and no `dispatch` event

, so the ledger can never show a task that never ran. |
| **Append-only ledger** | One JSON line per
decision. History is never rewritten or deleted, and it can be queried, diffed and audited by somet

hing that is not an LLM. |
| **Pluggable execution bodies** | The plane picks no model and does not

care which command runs a card. Swap the command, keep the governance. |
| **Unparsed dependencies a
re fatal** | A dependency marker that cannot be parsed refuses the dispatch. It is never silently dr
** | A dependency marker that cannot be parsed refuses the dispatch. It is never silently dropped. |
## Scope

**A personal tool, not an enterprise platform.** foreman-plane is deliberately
small. It is designed

for **one person, one machine, one state directory** — not
for a team, a fleet or a regulated org.

Saying this out loud is part of the
design: a tool that pretends to be a platform costs you more in

configuration
than it saves.
**What it is**

- A plain process. Start it when you need it, stop it when you are done.
- One directory of state (`

FOREMAN_HOME`) and one append-only JSONL ledger.
- A handful of interchangeable CLI agents, a few re

positories, one task graph.
- State you can read with `cat` and `jq` — no service account, no propri

one task graph.
- State you can read with `cat` and `jq` — no service account, no proprietary store.
**What it is not, and is not going to grow into**
| Not this | Why — and what to use instead |
| A multi-tenant platform | No tenancy, no RBAC, no SSO, no audit export. One `FOREMAN_HOME` belongs

to one person. |
| A durable workflow engine | No daemon, no queue broker, no timers, no HA, no ret

ries at scale. For resumable long-running workflows use Temporal, Airflow or Argo Workflows. |
| A d
atabase | The ledger is a JSONL file — fast and auditable at the scale of one person's tasks, not a

sharded store with a query planner. |
| An enterprise audit product | No retention policy engine, no

signed reports, no compliance controls. |
| A place for business logic | The plane decides nothing.

Your agent owns the work; the plane owns the sequence, the gate and the verdict. |
| A dashboard |
The whole surface is CLI, MCP stdio and a Python API. There is no UI and no web server. |
**Why this is a feature**

The tool fits in one directory, starts in milliseconds, and can be read end to
end with a text edito

r. If your requirement is "our forty-person org needs
approval workflows with SLA clocks and a Postg

res-backed audit trail", this is
the wrong tool and you should not spend an afternoon on it. If it i

s "my agents
keep forgetting what they promised last week and I want a ledger that says so",
it is e
xactly the right size.

## What it feels like

> You: `Finish these reports first, then let the downstream job merge them.`
>
> foreman-plane: Thre

e cards. The downstream one carries `[depends_on]`, so it
> cannot even start while the upstream fil

es are missing. When everything is
> done the artefacts get checked again, a missing field means `fa

il`, and the
> ledger records which file fell short.
## Install

You get two identical commands — use whichever you like:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

There is deliberately **no `foreman` command**. That name is already taken by
other projects — an AI

orchestration engine on npm, an infrastructure manager
on GitHub — and two packages shipping the sa

me binary name is a real conflict
[该节后续省略]
### Who decides what gets dispatched

**The plane never decides.** It has no planner, no model, no priority queue
and no scheduler. It exe

cutes the cards it is handed and refuses the ones
whose hard dependencies are not met yet.
[代码示例省略，未执行]

A blocked card is **not** woken up automatically: once the upstream passes,
the orchestrator (or you

) submits the card again. `blocked` is deliberately
not `dispatched`, so a blocked task stays re-dis

patchable — otherwise the task
graph would deadlock and the upstream could never unblock it.
### What foreman-plane does not do

* No daemon, no scheduler, no cron, no HTTP API, no port to open.
* It does not choose an agent, a m

odel or a priority.
* It does not retry a blocked card for you.
* It does not believe the model abou
t the outcome — only files.

For where this stops being the right tool, see
Scope.
